parsed.explanation: No trans-specific offence, no facility/bathroom rule, no custody-placement, strip-search or police-targeting finding, and no documented anti-trans violence or service refusals. The heaviest documented fact is the colonial-era male same-sex felony statute (14/7/5 years); it is not trans law, but a trans woman read as male and having sex with a man falls within its scope, so it is a real, conditional, severe exposure rather than a dead letter proven safe. Enforcement is documented as absent only to 2013 — a dated absence, not present safety. Offsetting climate signals: an embedded gender-diverse tradition (pinapinaaine), no history of government abuse, and 2011 UN SOGI statement support. No gender-identity protection, no hate-crime recourse, no service-remedy record; these are resident gaps and light, but they leave the visitor with no working remedy. Borders, custody and ward practice are unanswered questions, not shown exposures. Sits below the 0.65 Valess anchor (which has documented acceptance and an operating court remedy) and above the 0.45 anchors (no documented universal exposure or scale-level discrimination).
